title: Make a Kindness Jar
description: Fill a jar with little paper slips, each naming one kind thing to do. Every day, pull one out and do it. Kindness becomes a daily habit — and a daily surprise.

body.heading: How it works
paragraphs: First, make the jar pretty. Stick some paper shapes or drawings on the outside, and give it a name, like “Our Kindness Jar”. Then, with an adult, write kind deeds on small slips of paper. Keep them simple: “Draw a picture for Grandma.” “Help set the table.” “Say one kind thing to a friend.” “Share a toy.” Fold each slip and pop it in the jar.
Every morning, or at dinner time, one person pulls a slip out of the jar. That is the day's kind deed. Do it together if you like — kindness is even better shared.

body.heading: Make it a habit
paragraphs: At the end of the week, sit together and talk about the slips you pulled. Which one was the easiest? Which one made someone smile the most? Which one would you like to do again? Write new slips to replace the ones you used, so the jar never runs empty.
You can also add slips for kind words, not just kind deeds: “Tell Dad one thing you love about him.” “Thank the bus driver.” A jar full of kind words is a jar full of good days.

takeaway: A jar full of kind deeds makes kindness a daily habit.
materials: A clean jar with a lid
Pens or pencils, and stickers or coloured paper to decorate the jar
supervision: An adult helps the child write the slips, reads them together each week, and keeps the jar in a shared family space.
safetyNotes: Use a plastic jar, or keep a glass jar on a high shelf out of reach of toddlers
Keep small paper slips away from babies and toddlers, who might put them in their mouths
screenFreeExtension: At dinner once a week, pull out three slips and act out one kind deed together as a family.
